The same command as [Graphics](Graphics), under the name that 3D programs use. There is no 2D-only graphics mode, so the 3D commands work after either of them, and a program that opens its window with `Graphics` can use 3D commands as well. It has to be the first graphics command of a program: every drawing command fails until it ran. After it, the back buffer is the target of drawing and you draw one frame at a time with [RenderWorld](RenderWorld) and [Flip](Flip). Calling either of them again closes the window and opens a new one.

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| 0 | Window. This is the default. |
| 1 | Full screen. |
| 2 | Window. |
| 3 | Window whose size can be changed by the user; the picture is scaled to fit. |
| 4 | Window without a border: no title bar and no frame. This is a BlitzLLVM extension that original Blitz does not have. |

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 640, 480, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
cube = CreateCube()
PositionEntity cube, 0, 0, 5

While Not KeyHit(1)
	TurnEntity cube, 1, 2, 0
	RenderWorld
	Flip
Wend
```
@param width  Width of the picture in pixels.
@param height  Height of the picture in pixels.
@param depth  Color depth, which picks the format of the buffers: 8 for a palette of 256 colors (see [GraphicsPalette](GraphicsPalette)), 12 for R4G4B4A4, 15 for A1R5G5B5, 16 for R5G6B5, 24 for R8G8B8X8, 30 for R10G10B10A2, 32 for R8G8B8A8 and 64 for R16G16B16A16 (half precision floats, never integers). 0 gives 32. Defaults to 0.
@param mode  Window or full screen as in the table. Defaults to 0.
@gap Unlike in Blitz3D, mode 0 always opens a window, and `Graphics` and `Graphics3D` are the same command. The 3D commands do not need `Graphics3D` in particular.
@gap The depth does not pick a video mode, it picks the format of the buffers: 8 is a palette of 256 colors, 12 is R4G4B4A4, 15 is A1R5G5B5, 16 is R5G6B5, 24 is R8G8B8X8, 30 is R10G10B10A2, 32 is R8G8B8A8 and 64 is R16G16B16A16 with half precision floats. 0 and any other number give 32 (with a warning for the others), and a format that the graphics card can't draw to gives the next smaller one. Pixels are read and written as 8 bits per channel whatever the depth is. See [Color depth](Color-Depth).
@gap Full screen (mode 1) does not change the video mode of the display: the picture is shown at the largest size that fits with its aspect ratio kept, and the rest is black. See [Fullscreen](Fullscreen).
@gap A window without a border (mode 4) has the size you ask for and cannot be resized by the user.
